summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was readmitted two days after discharge due to fever, rigors, and lethargy. She was diagnosed with E. coli urosepsis, confirmed by positive urine culture. She responded well to IV meropenem, with resolution of fever and improved mental status. An echocardiogram showed improved left ventricular function with an ejection fraction over 55%, and telemetry revealed intermittent left bundle branch block. A PICC line was placed for continued antibiotic therapy. Her immunosuppressive regimen was adjusted, and she was started on carvedilol for heart protection. She was discharged to a rehabilitation facility to complete her antibiotic course with close follow-up planned for her heart and kidney function.
